title: Cells
standard_text: Investigate the structure and function of cells as the basic units of living things, comparing plant and animal cells and describing specialised cells; use light microscopes (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 8 science worksheets on cells: cell theory, plant and animal cell structures, specialised cells and using a light microscope to calculate magnification. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Cells are the building blocks of life.
key_sub: Plant cells have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole; animal cells do not.
body_html:
How to think about it

All living things are made of cells, and every cell comes from another cell.

  • Animal and plant cells: nucleus, cytoplasm, cell membrane, mitochondria. Plant cells also: cell wall, chloroplasts, large vacuole.
  • Specialised cells have shapes that suit their jobs: red blood cells, nerve cells, root hair cells, sperm cells.
  • Total magnification = eyepiece × objective. Real size = image size ÷ magnification.
Example

10× eyepiece and 40× objective?

multiply

Answer: 400×

Example

Green, cell wall, big vacuole. Plant or animal?

chloroplasts and a cell wall

Answer: plant

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all cells have a cell wall and chloroplasts.
  • Mixing up the cell membrane and the cell wall.
  • Adding the lens values instead of multiplying them.

faq.q: What are the main differences between plant and animal cells?
faq.a: Plant cells have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large permanent vacuole. Animal cells do not, but both have a nucleus, cytoplasm, a membrane and mitochondria.
Multiply the eyepiece by the objective lens: 10× × 40× = 400×. To find real size, divide the image size by the magnification.
A cell with a special shape or structure for its job, such as a nerve cell that is long and thin to carry messages.

items.q: Matilda makes a list of organisms. Which one is multicellular?
items.e: Multicellular organisms are made of many cells, often of different types.

items.q: What does unicellular mean?
c: made of two kinds of cells
items.e: Bacteria are unicellular.

items.q: Noah says, “If it is made of cells, it is alive.” Which of these is made of cells?
items.e: All living things are made of one or more cells.

items.q: Ethan sorts objects. Which one is NOT made of cells?
items.e: Nonliving things are not made of cells. (A virus is not a cell; it cannot live on its own.)

items.q: Kai makes a list of organisms. Which one is multicellular?
items.e: Multicellular organisms are made of many cells, often of different types.

items.q: Lachlan says, “If it is made of cells, it is alive.” Which of these is made of cells?
items.e: All living things are made of one or more cells.

items.q: A human skin cell is about 30 micrometers wide. Under a 100× microscope, about how wide does it appear?
items.e: 30 micrometers × 100 = 3000 micrometers, or about 3 mm (1 mm = 1000 micrometers).

items.q: What does the cell theory say?
c: Only animals are made of cells.
All living things are made of cells, cells are the basic unit of life, and new cells come from existing cells.
Cells are found only in plants.
items.e: These three ideas were built from many microscope observations.

items.q: Priya looks at pond water under a microscope. Which organism is made of only one cell?
items.e: Unicellular organisms, like bacteria, amoebas and yeast, are made of a single cell.

items.q: Who first used the word 'cell' after looking at cork under an early microscope?
items.e: Better microscopes later let scientists see the nucleus and other parts.

items.q: A microscope has a 10× eyepiece and a 40× objective lens. What is the total magnification?
items.e: Multiply the two values: 10 × 40 = 400.

items.q: What is a cell?
c: the smallest unit that can carry out all the processes of life
items.e: Cells are the building blocks of living things.

items.q: An amoeba is about 400 micrometers wide. Under a 400× microscope, about how wide does it appear?
items.e: 400 micrometers × 400 = 160 000 micrometers, or about 160 mm (1 mm = 1000 micrometers).

items.q: An amoeba is about 400 micrometers wide. Under a 100× microscope, about how wide does it appear?
items.e: 400 micrometers × 100 = 40 000 micrometers, or about 40 mm (1 mm = 1000 micrometers).

items.q: Priya sorts objects. Which one is NOT made of cells?
items.e: Nonliving things are not made of cells. (A virus is not a cell; it cannot live on its own.)

items.q: Where does respiration take place in a cell?
items.e: Mitochondria release energy from glucose.

items.q: What is the job of the cell membrane?
c: controls what enters and leaves the cell
gives the plant cell a rigid shape
items.e: The membrane is selectively permeable.

items.q: Where does photosynthesis take place?
items.e: Chloroplasts contain green chlorophyll.

items.q: Which part is partially permeable and controls the movement of substances in and out of the cell?
items.e: The cell wall is fully permeable.

items.q: William looks at pond water under a microscope. Which organism is made of only one cell?
items.e: Unicellular organisms, like bacteria, amoebas and yeast, are made of a single cell.

items.q: This is a plant cell. Which part is labelled A?
items.e: Follow each line to the part it touches.

items.q: Priya is labelling a cell model. What is the main job of the chloroplasts?
c: Capture sunlight to make food (sugar) by photosynthesis
Controls what enters and leaves the cell
Controls the cell's activities and holds the genetic information (DNA)
items.e: The chloroplasts capture sunlight to make food (sugar) by photosynthesis.

items.q: Mei is labelling a cell model. What is the main job of the cytoplasm?
c: Controls what enters and leaves the cell
A jelly-like fluid that holds the other parts
Capture sunlight to make food (sugar) by photosynthesis
A stiff outer layer that supports and protects a plant cell
items.e: The cytoplasm a jelly-like fluid that holds the other parts.

items.q: Zara is labelling a cell model. What is the main job of the mitochondria?
c: Release energy from food (sugar) for the cell to use
Controls the cell's activities and holds the genetic information (DNA)
Controls what enters and leaves the cell
items.e: The mitochondria release energy from food (sugar) for the cell to use.

items.q: Which structures are found in plant cells but not animal cells?
c: cell wall, chloroplasts and a large permanent vacuole
items.e: Both have a nucleus, cytoplasm, membrane and mitochondria.

items.q: Ethan's notes say one cell part captures sunlight to make food (sugar) by photosynthesis. Which part is it?
items.e: The chloroplasts capture sunlight to make food (sugar) by photosynthesis.

items.q: Why is a cover slip placed on a slide?
c: to hold the specimen flat and stop it drying out
items.e: Lower it carefully to avoid air bubbles.

items.q: This is a plant cell. Which letter labels the cell membrane?
items.e: Follow each line to the part it touches.

items.q: This is a plant cell. Which part is labelled A?
items.e: Follow each line to the part it touches.

items.q: William's notes describe a jelly-like fluid that holds the other parts. Which part is it?
items.e: The cytoplasm a jelly-like fluid that holds the other parts.

items.q: What does cell theory state?
c: Cells are made of living things.
All living things are made of cells, cells are the basic unit of life, and new cells come from existing cells.
items.e: Cell theory came from many scientists' observations.

items.q: Ruby's notes say one cell part controls what enters and leaves the cell. Which part is it?
items.e: The cell membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell.

items.q: Tom's notes say one cell part controls the cell's activities and holds the genetic information (DNA). Which part is it?
items.e: The nucleus controls the cell's activities and holds the genetic information (DNA).

items.q: Jack is labelling a cell model. What is the main job of the vacuole?
c: Controls what enters and leaves the cell
A stiff outer layer that supports and protects a plant cell
A jelly-like fluid that holds the other parts
items.e: The vacuole stores water and other materials.

items.q: Sienna is labelling a cell model. What is the main job of the cell membrane?
c: A stiff outer layer that supports and protects a plant cell
Controls what enters and leaves the cell
A jelly-like fluid that holds the other parts
items.e: The cell membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell.

items.q: Why do we stain cells before looking at them under a microscope?
c: to make parts such as the nucleus easier to see
items.e: Iodine and methylene blue are common stains.

items.q: This is an animal cell. Which letter labels the cell membrane?
items.e: Follow each line to the part it touches.

items.q: This is an animal cell. Which letter labels a mitochondrion?
items.e: Follow each line to the part it touches.

items.q: This is an animal cell. Which part is labelled B?
items.e: Follow each line to the part it touches.

items.q: What is the job of the nucleus?
c: contains genetic information (DNA) and controls the cell
items.e: It is the control centre.

items.q: In this animal cell model, which labelled part is a jelly-like fluid that holds the other parts?
items.e: That part is the cytoplasm.

items.q: This is a model of an animal cell. Which letter points to the mitochondria?
items.e: The mitochondria releases energy from food (sugar) for the cell to use.

items.q: A cell has a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole. What kind of cell is it?
items.e: Cell walls and chloroplasts are found in plant cells; root cells do not get light, so they have no chloroplasts.

items.q: Where are the mitochondria found: in animal cells, plant cells or both?
items.e: Plant cells have everything animal cells have, plus a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole.

items.q: Where is a large permanent vacuole found: in animal cells, plant cells or both?
items.e: Plant cells have everything animal cells have, plus a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole.

items.q: A cell has a cell wall and many chloroplasts, and comes from a leaf. What kind of cell is it most likely to be?
c: a bacterium with no genetic material
items.e: Leaf cells make food in their chloroplasts.

items.q: Where are the chloroplasts found: in animal cells, plant cells or both?
items.e: Plant cells have everything animal cells have, plus a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole.

items.q: A cell is round, has no cell wall and carries oxygen in the blood. What kind of cell is it most likely to be?
c: a bacterium with no genetic material
items.e: A red blood cell is an animal cell.

items.q: A cell from a carrot root has a cell wall but no chloroplasts. What kind of cell is it?
c: a plant cell that does not get sunlight
items.e: Cell walls and chloroplasts are found in plant cells; root cells do not get light, so they have no chloroplasts.

items.q: A cell has a long tail, a nucleus and no cell wall. What kind of cell is it most likely to be?
c: a bacterium with no genetic material
items.e: A sperm cell is an animal cell.

items.q: Which part is found in plant cells but NOT in animal cells?
items.e: Only plant cells have a cell wall and chloroplasts.

items.q: Where is the cytoplasm found: in animal cells, plant cells or both?
items.e: Plant cells have everything animal cells have, plus a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole.

items.q: Which part is found in BOTH plant and animal cells?
c: the cell wall and chloroplasts only
items.e: Both plant and animal cells have a nucleus, cell membrane, cytoplasm and mitochondria.

items.q: Which part is found in plant cells but NOT in animal cells?
items.e: Only plant cells have a cell wall and chloroplasts.

items.q: A cell has a cell wall, a large central vacuole and chloroplasts. What kind of cell is it most likely to be?
c: a bacterium with no genetic material
items.e: Only plant cells have a cell wall and chloroplasts.

items.q: In this plant cell model, which labelled part releases energy from food (sugar) for the cell to use?
items.e: That part is the mitochondria.

items.q: This is a model of a plant cell. Which letter points to the chloroplasts?
items.e: The chloroplasts captures sunlight to make food (sugar) by photosynthesis.

items.q: Where is the nucleus found: in animal cells, plant cells or both?
items.e: Plant cells have everything animal cells have, plus a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole.

items.q: Which part is found in BOTH plant and animal cells?
c: the cell wall and chloroplasts only
items.e: Both plant and animal cells have a nucleus, cell membrane, cytoplasm and mitochondria.

items.q: A cell has a nucleus, mitochondria and a cell membrane, but no cell wall and no chloroplasts. What kind of cell is it most likely?
c: a cell from a pine needle
items.e: Cell walls and chloroplasts are found in plant cells; root cells do not get light, so they have no chloroplasts.

items.q: Which specialised cell has tiny hairs that sweep mucus out of the airways?
items.e: Specialised cells have features that suit their jobs.

items.q: How is a root hair cell adapted for its job?
c: It has tiny hairs that sweep mucus out of the airways.
It is packed with chloroplasts for photosynthesis.
It has a long, thin hair to take in water from the soil.
It has a tail to swim to the egg.
items.e: Specialised cells have features that suit their jobs.

items.q: Which specialised cell has a long, thin hair to take in water from the soil?
items.e: Specialised cells have features that suit their jobs.

items.q: By diffusion, which way does ink move here: from the drop or through the water?
c: through the water into the drop
from the drop through the water
it does not move at all
items.e: Particles diffuse from where there are a lot of them (high concentration) to where there are fewer (low concentration).

items.q: Why are plant leaves green?
c: Their cells contain chloroplasts with green chlorophyll.
items.e: Chlorophyll absorbs light.

items.q: Cell A has 8 units of a dye and cell B has 9 units. Which way will the dye diffuse?
c: it will move both ways equally for ever
from cell B to cell A
from cell A to cell B
items.e: Diffusion goes from high to low concentration.

items.q: Cell A has 7 units of carbon dioxide and cell B has 25 units. Which way will carbon dioxide diffuse?
c: from cell B to cell A
from cell A to cell B
it will move both ways equally for ever
items.e: Diffusion goes from high to low concentration.

items.q: What is a cell?
c: the smallest unit of a living organism
items.e: All living things are made of cells.

items.q: Which specialised cell carries oxygen around the body?
items.e: It has no nucleus and is packed with haemoglobin.

items.q: Cell A has 14 units of oxygen and cell B has 13 units. Which way will oxygen diffuse?
c: it will move both ways equally for ever
from cell A to cell B
from cell B to cell A
items.e: Diffusion goes from high to low concentration.

items.q: By diffusion, which way does carbon dioxide move here: from muscle cells or into the blood?
c: from the blood into muscle cells
it does not move at all
from muscle cells into the blood
items.e: Particles diffuse from where there are a lot of them (high concentration) to where there are fewer (low concentration).

items.q: Which specialised cell is long with branches to carry electrical messages?
items.e: Specialised cells have features that suit their jobs.

items.q: By diffusion, which way does glucose move here: from the blood or into body cells?
c: from body cells into the blood
from the blood into body cells
it does not move at all
items.e: Particles diffuse from where there are a lot of them (high concentration) to where there are fewer (low concentration).

items.q: Who first saw and named cells, using a microscope in 1665?
items.e: He looked at cork.

items.q: How is an egg cell adapted for its job?
c: It is long with branches to carry electrical messages.
It has tiny hairs that sweep mucus out of the airways.
It is packed with chloroplasts for photosynthesis.
It is large and contains a food store for the growing embryo.
items.e: Specialised cells have features that suit their jobs.

items.q: Cell A has 17 units of glucose and cell B has 7 units. Which way will glucose diffuse?
c: from cell A to cell B
from cell B to cell A
it will move both ways equally for ever
items.e: Diffusion goes from high to low concentration.

items.q: How is a palisade leaf cell adapted for its job?
c: It is large and contains a food store for the growing embryo.
It has a long, thin hair to take in water from the soil.
It is long with branches to carry electrical messages.
It is packed with chloroplasts for photosynthesis.
items.e: Specialised cells have features that suit their jobs.

items.q: Which part of the cell contains DNA?
items.e: Genetic information.

items.q: What is the cell wall of a plant made of?
items.e: Strong fibres.

items.q: Which specialised cell has lots of mitochondria and can contract?
items.e: Specialised cells have features that suit their jobs.

items.q: Which part of a light microscope is the knob that moves the stage a lot to get the image roughly in focus?
items.e: Learn the parts of the microscope.

items.q: Jack measures a cell as 4 mm wide in a photo magnified 400×. What is its real width?
items.e: Real size = image size ÷ magnification = 4 ÷ 400.

items.q: Why should you never use a mirror to reflect direct sunlight into a microscope?
items.e: Safety.

items.q: In Mia's model, the bag stands for the cell membrane. What could she add to model a plant cell?
c: nothing; plant cells are the same
a stiff box around the bag for the cell wall, and green beads for chloroplasts
items.e: Plant cells also have a cell wall and chloroplasts.

items.q: A cell has a cell wall but no chloroplasts. Where might it come from?
c: a leaf surface in the sun
items.e: Root cells.

items.q: Which part of a light microscope is the flat platform where the slide is placed?
items.e: Learn the parts of the microscope.

items.q: Amelia looks at an Elodea leaf under a microscope and sees green dots moving around. What are the green dots?
items.e: Chloroplasts are green and easy to see in leaf cells.

items.q: A microscope gives a total magnification of ×1500 with a ×100 objective lens. What is the eyepiece magnification?
items.e: Eyepiece = total ÷ objective = 1500 ÷ 100 = 15.

items.q: Why should onion cells be stained with iodine?
c: It makes the onion taste better.
Iodine stains the nucleus and cell wall so they are easier to see.
items.e: Staining increases contrast.

items.q: Ella sees no chloroplasts in onion skin cells, even though onions are plants. Why?
c: Onion bulbs grow underground and do not photosynthesise.
items.e: Not every plant cell has chloroplasts.

items.q: Kai sees bubbles under the cover slip. How could he avoid this next time?
c: lower the cover slip slowly at an angle
items.e: This pushes air out.

items.q: Ruby's slide is blurry at 400×. What should she adjust?
c: the coarse focus knob at high power
items.e: At high power, only use fine focus.

items.q: Which part of a light microscope is the lens you look through?
items.e: Learn the parts of the microscope.

items.q: A microscope has a ×10 eyepiece lens and a ×4 objective lens. What is the total magnification?
items.e: Total magnification = eyepiece × objective = 10 × 4 = 40.

items.q: What is the fine focusing knob of a light microscope?
c: the knob that makes small changes to sharpen the image
the knob that moves the stage a lot to get the image roughly in focus
the lens just above the slide that you choose for low or high power
the flat platform where the slide is placed
items.e: Learn the parts of the microscope.

items.q: Mia sees cells with a green colour, a thick outer edge and a large central space. What are they most likely to be?
items.e: Chloroplasts, a cell wall and a vacuole are plant features.

items.q: A microscope gives a total magnification of ×150 with a ×10 objective lens. What is the eyepiece magnification?
items.e: Eyepiece = total ÷ objective = 150 ÷ 10 = 15.

items.q: What is the eyepiece lens of a light microscope?
c: the part that shines light up through the slide
the knob that makes small changes to sharpen the image
the lens just above the slide that you choose for low or high power
items.e: Learn the parts of the microscope.

items.q: A cell has a cell membrane, cytoplasm and a nucleus. Which conclusion is correct?
c: It must be a plant cell.
It must be an animal cell.
It is not a living cell.
It could be either a plant or an animal cell; more evidence is needed.
items.e: Both kinds of cell have these parts.

items.q: What is the stage of a light microscope?
c: the part that shines light up through the slide
the lens just above the slide that you choose for low or high power
the flat platform where the slide is placed
items.e: Learn the parts of the microscope.
